structured_output.world_model:
W3 (cost lens), after E025.

**Tip (E023).** E017 recipe cut to 9.0 true epochs (225 steps at batch 2000, 25 steps per epoch). Muon on the conv filters with 3 Newton-Schulz steps; filters are renormalized every step, so filter wd is inert. Lookahead/EMA with alpha ∝ t³. Resizing 24/28/32 px at 40/30/30% of steps. Widths 128/384/512, LS 0.3, SGD-group wd 0.006, CUDA graphs. Measured 6.198 s at 0.7538. My estimate of the true mean is about 0.753 ± 0.15 pp, which is on the bar.

**Time budget:** time ≈ F + V × (pixel fraction × steps/225), with F ≈ 0.5–0.6 s and V ≈ 7.4 s at 225 steps.
- Each 0.5 true epoch costs about 0.34 s (E020, E023), so 0.25 epoch is about 0.17 s.
- Pixel cuts save a bit more than their pixel share (E011, E018, E024: 26 px gave −0.13 s, more than I expected).
- MAC cuts return about half their share (E021).
- Convs already run near 150 TFLOP/s at 32 px, so kernel levers are spent.
- Group-1 MAC share is ~21%, and its backward is about 14% of conv work plus memory-bound BN/GELU backward at high resolution.

**Exchange rates (s saved per pp lost):**
- Epochs: about 3–6 s/pp.
- Last-group width: 1.6 s/pp.
- Dropping the 28 px phase: 1.6 s/pp.
- 26 px middle phase (E024): ~0.13 s for ~0.25 pp, worse than epochs.
- 20 px phase: 0.9 s/pp.

The binding constraint is margin. Each step of savings now needs a time-neutral accuracy gain to fund it, and none has been confirmed.

**Mechanisms:**
1. Lookahead endpoint averaging is worth ~1 pp (E005). The alpha ramp at ^2 gave +0.19 pp on 3 seeds (E025), within noise; at best a weak lever of ≤0.2 pp.
2. Muon gives ~+0.66 pp (E006). Its lr moves are flat (E014).
3. Accuracy is built in the mid- and high-resolution phases (E011, E018, E024). The 3×3-final-map regime theory is not supported: 26 px also lost accuracy.
4. Last-group width matters (E010); group 2 matters little (E021).
5. LS, wd and lr nudges are all noise (E013, E014, E016, E022, E025).

**Noise:**
- Per-seed std is ~0.3 pp, so the 3-seed SE is ~0.17 pp.
- Changing the step count re-rolls RNG.
- Time noise is ~0.5–1%.
- Deltas under 0.2 pp cannot be resolved without seeds 3–12.

**Misses:** I still under-forecast the time savings of resolution and schedule changes, and I forecast E025 above the tip's time (E017's level) when it ran at the tip's 6.20 s. Anchor time to the current tip, and correct savings upward by ~0.1 s.

**Unsure:**
- Whether loss-based example dropping beats a uniform epoch cut.
- Muon's critical batch size.
- Whether FreezeOut on group 1 is cheap in accuracy.
- PCIe transfer: my guess for the 40-seed mean is ~0.753, which clears the 0.75 bar.

forecasts.reason: No recipe change, so the numbers repeat the tip. My arithmetic puts 32 px convs near 150 TFLOP/s overall, though group 3 on small maps will be flagged.
E025 was discarded, so this is branch (b), −0.25 epoch: ~0.17 s saved for ~0.05–0.1 pp lost. The RNG re-roll makes clearing 0.753 a coin flip.
Skipping group-1 backward saves ~15–20% of ~1.85 s of tail time (~0.3 s). Freezing the high-resolution group early probably costs 0.1–0.3 pp.
Steps fall 9%, much like E020's epoch cut. Under LS 0.3 the loss ranking is mostly noise, so it acts as a slightly worse epoch trim.
20% fewer steps gives only ~2–3% less time, since the step is GPU-bound and pixel work is the same. Fewer Muon/EMA updates probably cost more than 0.15 pp.
Muon lr has been flat (E014). A gain of 0.2 pp on held-out seeds is unlikely; ×2 may even hurt.

cruxes: What is the held-out seeds 3–12 mean of the E023 tip? If it is under 0.753, every trim idea is infeasible and the loop needs a time-neutral accuracy gain first.
Does any time-neutral lever (alpha ramp ^2, BN recompute, Muon lr) show a held-out gain of at least 0.15 pp? That would fund a −0.25 to −0.5 epoch cut worth 0.17–0.34 s.
Is the group-1 backward really ≥15% of a 32 px step (I040 profile)? That decides whether FreezeOut (I043) can pay for its accuracy cost.
